identity.title: ALMA Observations of ρ-Oph 102: Grain Growth and Molecular Gas in the Disk around a Young Brown Dwarf

paper_type_evidence.quote: We present ALMA continuum and spectral line observations of the young Brown Dwarf $\rho$-Oph 102 at about 0.89 mm and 3.2 mm.

evidence.quote: a distance of 130 pc for the $\rho$-Oph SFR (cite: Wilking:2008; Lombardi:2008)
a distance of 130 pc for the $\rho$-Oph SFR (cite: Wilking:2008; Lombardi:2008)

question.value: Do disks around young brown dwarfs contain mm-sized grains and gas, as measured from the mm spectral index and CO emission for rho-Oph 102?

evidence.quote: In this Letter we report on our ALMA observations, which were designed to derive a solid estimate of the mm spectral index to constrain the dust properties.
This paper makes use of the following ALMA data: ADS/JAO.ALMA#2011.0.00259.S.

bands.value: Band 7 (~345 GHz) and Band 3 (~100 GHz), ALMA Cycle 0 Early Science

evidence.quote: We observed $\rho$–Oph 102 using ALMA Early Science in Cycle 0 at Band 7 and 3 (about 345 and 100 GHz, respectively).

frequencies_and_spectral_setup.value: four spectral windows of 1.875 GHz, 0.488 MHz channels; Band 7 centered 331.103, 332.998, 343.103, 344.998 GHz; Band 3 86.1021, 87.9976, 98.103, 99.999 GHz

evidence.quote: Spectral windows were centered at 331.103, 332.998, 343.103, 344.998 GHz for Band 7 observations and 86.1021, 87.9976, 98.103, 99.999 GHz for Band 3.
The only line emission detected was the CO ($J=3-2$) rotational line in Band 7 which was imaged separately.

configurations.value: Band 7: Compact (15 antennas, 2011 Nov 3) and Extended (16 antennas, 2012 May 23); Band 3: Extended (16 antennas, 2012 May 8)

evidence.quote: Observations in Band 7 were performed using 15 antennas in the Compact array configuration on November 3, 2011, and 16 antennas in the Extended array configuration on May 23, 2012

baselines.value: Band 7: shadowing limit to ~400 m; Band 3: ~35 to ~402 m

evidence.quote: Observations in Band 3 were conducted with 16 antennas in the Extended configuration on May 8, 2012 (projected baseline lengths from $\sim$35 to $\sim$402 m).
Considering our angular resolution of $\sim 0.6''$ at 0.89 mm
The total integration times on $\rho$–Oph 102 were approximately 15 and 30 minutes in Band 7 and 3, respectively.

evidence.quote: The interferometric visibility data were reduced using the CASA package (cite: McMullin:2007).

resulting in an accuracy of $\sim10\%$

task.value: CASA imaging; continuum with natural weighting using all line-free channels

evidence.quote: For each band, a continuum map was produced using natural weighting and combining all the channels without line emission.

weighting_robust.value: CO: natural weighting plus Gaussian taper (all data); robust weighting for baselines >~60 kλ (robust value not stated)

evidence.quote: we also imaged the data from baselines exceeding $\sim60$ k$\lambda$

uv_taper.value: Gaussian taper for extended CO map (value not stated)

evidence.quote: we first used all the data, natural weighting and a gaussian taper of the visibilities

what.value: Unresolved-disk photometry modeling procedure, adapted for BDs

evidence.quote: Our analysis of the unresolved disk photometry follows the procedure outlined in (cite: Testi:2001), adapted for the case of young BDs.
we model the mm continuum emission using a two-layer (surface$+$midplane) model of a flared disk heated by the radiation of the central BD (cite: Chiang:1997; Dullemond:2001).

what.value: Sub-stellar photospheric properties and dust model described in Figure 4 caption (not in text)

evidence.quote: The adopted sub-stellar photospheric properties of $\rho$-Oph 102 and the dust model are described in the caption of Figure [4](#fig:models).

analysis_steps.goal: image continuum and measure flux densities and spectral index

method.value: Natural-weighted continuum maps in each band; flux densities measured; spectral index from the two fluxes

validation.value: rms noise consistent with theoretical expectations

evidence.quote: The obtained rms-noise levels are consistent with the theoretical expectations given the on-source integration times.

analysis_steps.goal: test whether the continuum is resolved

method.value: Inspect visibility amplitude vs projected baseline; no decrease implies unresolved, size upper limit ~40 AU

evidence.quote: We conclude that our observations did not spatially resolve the disk continuum emission.

evidence.quote: The disk is detected at a $> 10\sigma$ level, with a velocity-integrated total flux of about $530 \pm 45$ mJy$\cdot$km/s.

findings_qualitative.value: CO emission detected from the disk, tentative velocity gradient ~1 km/s consistent with Keplerian rotation

claims.hypothesis: Do BD disks contain mm-sized grains?
claims.experiment: Two-band continuum spectral index plus disk modeling
claims.finding: mm-sized grains exist in the BD disk outer regions, challenging dust evolution models

evidence.quote: Our result indicates that mm-grains are found not only in the outer regions of T Tauri disks, but even in the low density environments of Brown Dwarf disks

claims.hypothesis: Is the BD disk gas-rich with similar relative mass as T Tauri disks?
claims.experiment: CO(3-2) mapping and dust mass with gas-to-dust 100
claims.result: CO detected >10σ; disk mass 0.3-1% of BD
claims.finding: Gas-rich disk with typical relative mass

evidence.quote: We derived a disk mass of $\sim 0.3-1$% of the mass of the Brown Dwarf

alternatives_considered_or_rejected.value: Small (<5 AU) optically thick disk rejected since it would need gas temperature >400 K

evidence.quote: This would correspond to a gas temperature $>$ 400 K, which is much higher than expected for a BD disk.

limitations_admitted.value: Disk unresolved so radius and inclination poorly constrained; CO extended emission affected by missing flux

evidence.quote: Since our observations did not allow us to spatially resolve the dust emission of the disk, we could not strongly constrain the disk radius and inclination.

referee_caveats_inferred: Only two continuum points; beta depends on assumed disk model and opacity
Assumed gas-to-dust 100 and CO optically thick/temperature argument are uncertain
